notes: Cover panel re-shoot of jalebi-15-hara: standing, full length, headroom for the tall crop.
prompt: Editorial fashion photograph for an Indian handloom label's festive lookbook. Tall vertical 9:16 frame.
GARMENT (a real product; match the reference photos exactly, including colours, borders and motifs):

- Kurta: the sleeveless viscose kurta from the references, in broad vertical stripes of bottle green and teal, with a deep V neckline, side pockets and a small gold embroidered motif near the pocket. Knee length.
- Trousers: the straight magenta-purple trousers from the references.
- It is a two-piece set: the kurta and the matching straight trousers shown in the references, worn together exactly as styled there.
MUSE: a woman in her early thirties with shoulder-length curly hair, gold hoops, stacked gold bangles, a relaxed easy smile, looking to the side as she walks.
MOMENT AND PLACE: Morning in a phool bazaar lane: she stands with marigold and tuberose garlands draped over her arm, flower stalls and baskets softly blurred on both sides of the lane behind her.
LIGHT: Soft morning haze with sunlight filtering down the lane; saturated marigold orange around the green.
COVER FRAMING (this photograph becomes one tall, narrow panel of the lookbook's opening page, behind a large title):
- POSE: she is standing upright, full length, head to toe in frame; ignore any seated or kneeling pose mentioned above.
- HEADROOM: the top quarter of the frame is calm, empty background (sky, wall, foliage or soft darkness); her head sits about a quarter of the way down, never near the top edge.
- Subject centred horizontally and filling the middle third of the width, so a narrow vertical crop keeps all of her.
- Keep the background simple and softly out of focus; nothing busy behind her face.
- CAMERA: eye level, 50mm lens at f/2.8, gentle depth of field, medium-format look with fine grain.
